clue.text: Panic — as might bird?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a state of nervous agitation
second meaning: what a bird does with its wings

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bird might panic like a person.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a verb phrase: a bird might beat its wings, so the answer completes 'as a bird might ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap is an everyday word for a fluster or panic, and it is also the wing movement of a bird.

clue.text: Twenty-one shillings for African country

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the old British gold coin worth one pound and one shilling
second meaning: the West African state

explanation.surface: A price of twenty-one shillings paid for an African country, as if a nation were bought cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: Before decimal currency a pound had twenty shillings; a guinea was a pound plus one shilling, a sum still used for some fees.
explanation.definitionFit: The guinea coin took its name from the gold of the Guinea coast, and the country keeps the same name.

clue.text: Computer unit to chew on, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: asks us to judge the word by how it is pronounced rather than how it is written

parts.note: to chew on something is to bite it

explanation.surface: A puzzling idea of a computer part you could chew.
explanation.definitionFit: A byte is the standard unit of digital storage, eight bits of data.

clue.text: Figure with cloth lifted up stone

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something up means reading it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a number, here ten
a rag is a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A statue with a cloth draped over it is hoisted up from a stone base.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnet is a deep red gemstone, so it is a precious stone.

clue.text: Muscle builders for young people, we hear?

indicators.note: signals that the words are to be judged by their spoken sound

parts.note: pro means in favour of, and teens are young people aged thirteen to nineteen

explanation.surface: A question about whether muscle-building supplements are meant for teenagers.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, 'pro teens' matches the answer's sound, though the second half is spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Proteins in the diet supply the amino acids from which the body repairs and grows muscle tissue.

clue.text: Chinese food bound to go on list

parts.note: to bound is to leap or spring
a roll is a list of names, as in a register

explanation.surface: A takeaway dish that is sure to appear on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to', but 'bound' is a leap and 'to go on' just places one part after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring roll is a fried pancake wrapper filled with vegetables, a staple of Chinese restaurant menus.

clue.text: Our silly cryptic, misleading

indicators.note: something cryptic is obscure and jumbled, so the letters are to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter admits that this silly puzzle of ours is misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illusory gives a false impression, deceiving the senses or the mind.

clue.text: Inward-looking person feels no different

indicators.note: a different version of the letters means an altered arrangement of them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An introvert claims to feel no different from anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun refers back to the self, the person one looks at when looking inward.

clue.text: Short part, but almost developed

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
something developed has been worked into a new form, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
the word but minus its last letter

explanation.surface: An actor's role was short but had nearly been fleshed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrupt can mean brief and curt, as in a short reply or sudden ending.

clue.text: Clean parasite

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to wipe with a soft absorbent pad
second meaning: a person who lives off others

explanation.walkthrough: The first is a verb, the second a noun: a cadger is called this because they soak up what others provide.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to wash with a sponge, and a sponge is also a scrounger who lives at others' expense.

clue.text: Clever chap, saint welcomed by German couple?

indicators.note: being welcomed by others means being taken in among them

parts.note: ein is German for one, so a couple is two of them
ST is the usual abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A bright fellow, a saintly one, is received warmly by a German pair.
explanation.walkthrough: The saint sits between the two German words for one; the question mark flags the playful reading of 'couple'.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein's name is used as a byword for a genius, so it fits a clever chap.

clue.text: Sign of commitment in battle arena

parts.note: an engagement is a military clash
a ring is an arena, as for boxing or a circus

explanation.surface: A display of dedication shown by a fighter in the arena.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring given when a couple agree to marry signals their commitment to each other.

clue.text: Certainly not OK, rather bizarre country

parts.note: an emphatic refusal

indicators.note: bizarre means weird and out of order, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A verdict on a state judged definitely not all right but rather strange.
explanation.definitionFit: North Korea is the nation occupying the northern half of the Korean peninsula.

clue.text: Cream in cornet I left upside down

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned upside down means reading the letters from bottom to top
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the run runs across the end of cornet, the I and the start of left, read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone describes ice cream in a cone that was left upturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream' looks like the dessert topping in a cornet, but it means the best of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, just as an elite is the select top group.

clue.text: Get a hold on complaint, briefly

indicators.note: making something brief means cutting it short at the end

parts.note: a gripe is a grumble

explanation.surface: Advice to take control of a grievance by keeping it short.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip is to grasp firmly, both literally and in the sense of mastering a problem.

clue.text: Institute protecting temporary accommodation in powerful manner

indicators.note: something protecting another wraps around it on all sides

parts.note: short for polytechnic, a British college of higher education
a tent is shelter put up for a short stay

explanation.surface: An organisation forcefully defends makeshift housing.
explanation.definitionFit: Potently means with great power or strong effect, an adverb matching the phrase.

clue.text: Leader of regime in charge, one's gathered

definitions.note: read as 'one is gathered': a thing that is gathered

indicators.note: in places one element inside the other

parts.note: to charge a glass is to fill it

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its head

parts.note: the opening letter of regime

explanation.surface: The head of a regime in power has collected supporters around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In charge' looks like a fixed phrase for being in power, but 'in' is the insertion and charge means to load.
explanation.definitionFit: A frill is a strip of fabric gathered along one edge to make a ruffled trim.

clue.text: Generous: not entirely reliable, unfortunately

indicators.note: not entirely means one letter short of the whole, so the last is lost
an unfortunate turn of events leaves things in disarray, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word reliable missing its final letter

explanation.surface: A grudging verdict on a person who is kind-hearted but cannot always be relied on.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean open-handed and lavish in giving, as in liberal helpings.

clue.text: Attempt photograph

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a go or try
second meaning: a picture taken with a camera

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like trying to take a picture; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a shot at something is an informal attempt, and a shot is also a single photo.

clue.text: A jam preserve, warmer at night?

parts.note: being in a jam is being in hot water, in trouble
to bottle fruit is to preserve it

explanation.surface: Jam and preserves sound like a pantry list, then turn into something cosy for the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' and 'preserve' look like fruit spreads, but jam is a predicament and preserve is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber bottle filled with hot water is put in a bed to warm it before sleep.

clue.text: A fair land

parts.note: taken as written
fair hair or skin is light in colour

explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to come down and settle, as a bird lands on a branch.

clue.text: Warm oven in Tipperary, emptied

indicators.note: in sets one element within the other
an emptied word has lost its contents, keeping only its first and last letters

parts.note: Tipperary is an Irish county
an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: A hot oven in an emptied house in the Irish county of Tipperary.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasty is an informal word for comfortably warm.

clue.text: Agree how Penny may possibly have died?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to correspond or happen together

definitions.text: how Penny may possibly have died
definitions.meaning: second, playful meaning: the killing of a coin, on the pattern of words like homicide

explanation.surface: A puzzled agreement about how a woman named Penny met her end.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a woman's name; read as the coin, the answer splits as a coin plus the -cide ending meaning killing.
explanation.definitionFit: To coincide is to agree or match exactly, as two accounts or dates can.

clue.text: Fixed by needle, a static point

indicators.note: something fixed by these words is held fast within them

parts.note: the run starts at the end of needle and ends early in static

explanation.surface: A compass needle points steadily to one fixed direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass needle in the surface is apt, since the answer is a point of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four cardinal points marked on a compass.

clue.text: Are you sure about supporter?

parts.note: re means concerning
an ally backs you up

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you are certain about a backer.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as a question, the word expresses doubt, asking whether the speaker is sure.

clue.text: Game bird

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bit of fun or a prank
second meaning: a songbird such as the skylark

explanation.walkthrough: 'Game bird' reads as a pheasant or grouse, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a carefree bit of fun, and also a small singing bird.

clue.text: Chap took a tumble I see!

parts.note: to fall is to take a tumble, in the past tense
an exclamation of understanding

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a man has fallen over.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellah is an informal spelling of fellow, a man or chap.

clue.text: One so bookish, not the Queen!

definitions.note: a noun: a person who lives alone

indicators.note: not the monarch means her usual abbreviation is to be taken out

parts.note: taken as written
fond of books and literature

explanation.surface: Someone is so studious, unlike the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen removed from the middle of the bookish word.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary is a recluse or hermit, a person who lives alone, so one by oneself.
